newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi says Moslems to mark haj climax on April 16.
newsitem.headline: Saudi says Moslems to mark haj climax on April 16.

text.p: Saudi Arabia on Tuesday announced April 16 would be the climax of the annual haj pilgrimage when an estimated two million Moslems will march to Mount Arafat, the site of the Prophet Mohammad's last sermon 14 centuries ago.
The following day would be the beginning of Eid al-Adha, when pilgrims symbolically stone the devil at a site on the outskirts of Mecca and slaughter sheep and cows.
The Saudi Press Agency issued the royal court announcement.
The haj is one of the five pillars of Islam and every Moslem who is able and can afford to perform it should do so at least once.
Pilgrims have been arriving in the kingdom for weeks. Saudi television shows footage every day of pilgrims walking around the Kaaba, a black cubic shrine in Mecca that is Islam's holiest site.
Circling the Kaaba is one of the key elements of the haj. Moslems face in the direction of the Kaaba to pray, wherever they are in the world.
